name: Makyura
description: The original Makyura the Destructor let its owner activate Traps from the hand after it reached the Graveyard. Exchange of the Spirit decks exploited that timing to threaten a win before the opponent had taken a turn.

defining_cards.name: Makyura the Destructor
defining_cards.why: Its original effect allowed Traps to be activated from the hand the turn it reached the Graveyard, accelerating otherwise slow draw combinations.

defining_cards.name: Card Destruction
defining_cards.why: Replacing both hands could disrupt an opponent holding a combo while loading the Graveyard for the player's own effects.

defining_cards.name: Exchange of the Spirit
defining_cards.why: Its original effect could swap an opponent's nearly empty Graveyard with their Deck, setting up a loss at their next required draw.

defining_cards.name: Temple of the Kings
defining_cards.why: The period version let its controller activate Traps on the turn they were set, speeding up Exchange of the Spirit.

defining_cards.name: Painful Choice
defining_cards.why: It sent four of five selected cards to the Graveyard, setting up revival and Graveyard effects even when the opponent chose the weakest card to keep.

other_deck_samples.relationship: The Japanese timeline lists Card of Safe Return Exodia alongside Yata-Lock, Exchange of the Spirit and Last Turn in January 2002. This May 28 build of that same competing strategy has 40 Main cards, all within the January 1 pool and limits. The list predates Makyura and does not measure Makyura play.
